recommendations: Use your Life & Career Skills to create a focused development plan for Learning & Innovation Skills: set 2–3 specific learning objectives, timelines, and short checkpoints to track progress.
Leverage your IT & Media Skills to access and apply digital learning resources and prototyping tools (e.g., online modules, collaboration platforms) that let you practice new ideas quickly.
Adopt a short-cycle practice-feedback loop: try small experiments to apply new approaches, gather quick feedback, reflect, and iterate. Keep each cycle to 1–2 weeks to build learning agility.
Leverage your IT & Media Skills (4.10) to create small, demonstrable projects that require iterative problem solving — use these projects to practice and record learning processes.

Set focused, short-term learning goals to strengthen Learning & Innovation Skills (3.00): define one concrete objective, try an experiment, and capture what you learned and what you'd change next time.
Use digital tools you are strong with to structure and show Life & Career Skills (3.50): plan tasks, communicate progress, and keep simple evidence of planning, time management, and collaboration.

Leverage your Learning & Innovation strengths to structure short, focused learning cycles: pick a specific IT/media skill to practice in 1–4 week sprints, use reflection to consolidate learning, and adjust the next sprint based on what worked.

Address Life & Career Skills with a concise career routine: define 2–3 short-term SMART goals (career readiness, communication, time management), schedule weekly 30–60 minute action and reflection sessions, and use brief role-plays or mock interviews to practice professional interactions.

Seek regular, specific feedback: after completing micro-project milestones, request concrete feedback from a peer, mentor, or instructor to guide next steps for both IT & Media tasks and career-skill practice.
